headline: Flat sales, softer margins, and a deal to exit China
summary_short: A. O. Smith's Q3 2026 sales were $940.5 million, flat y/y, with diluted EPS of $0.93 versus $0.94 a year ago; it agreed to sell 81% of its China business and cut its full-year outlook basis to exclude China.
summary_long: Net sales of $940.5 million were flat y/y. North America sales rose 3% to $761.6 million on boiler growth, pricing and the Leonard Valve acquisition, while Rest of World fell 7% on weak China demand. North America segment margin slipped to 23.6% from 24.2%. Net earnings were $126.3 million. The company agreed to sell an 81% stake in China to CPE, valuing it near $400 million. Guidance now excludes China: net sales growth of about 4% and adjusted EPS of $3.42-$3.52. Year-to-date free cash flow rose 4% to $396 million.
confidence_notes: Q3 results still include the China business; guidance is restated excluding China, so it is not comparable with prior guidance. Guidance entries were not written to the event shard (no sanctioned script for guidance writes). Adjusted EPS guidance excludes about $20 million of pre-tax North America water treatment restructuring and impairment.

drivers.explanation: North America gains from boilers, pricing and Leonard Valve were offset by lower residential water heater volumes and a 17% local-currency drop in China sales.
North America margin fell 60 basis points on lower residential water heater volumes and higher steel and freight costs, partly offset by tariff refunds and pricing.
Interest expense rose to $7.7 million from $3.6 million after a term loan funded the Leonard Valve purchase, adding to lower Rest of World earnings.
Management cited inflation, softer North American residential demand and China weakness, and said the China sale lets it focus capital on higher-return areas.
